quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back of the group.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane collects oil and becomes slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for better traction. Also slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is applied.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
Applies even braking for both the front and rear brakes when either is applied.
Learns and remembers the approximate braking force used by the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system automatically applies some front brake force when you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so approaching drivers can see the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever firmly and smoothly with all four fingers, gradually increasing pressure.

questions.question: If you need to brake while going around a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are not in the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Your tires have less grip when the motorcycle is leaning. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Try to straighten up before braking.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: A child does not have to reach the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the operator. A child in front may not balance well and could block your controls.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Block access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen. It should keep you away from other drivers' blind spots and surface hazards. It should also give you an escape route in case of danger.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of the following is NOT important?
questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards. It should fit snugly and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Do not worry about where you are in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: What is the safest way to cross angled railroad tracks?
questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight in your lane.
questions.explanation: The safest way is to go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to reach a right angle can be dangerous because it may move you into another lane.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders in a group communicate. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down quickly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down quickly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as bright as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice it, especially when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and whether they have eaten may also affect BAC.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than a walk, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn causes you to lean the right way.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning in a curve?

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be very careful. Your tire's traction is used partly for turning while leaning, so less traction is available for braking.

questions.question: What formation should a group use when exiting a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding on most roads. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly, then gradually add front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week. This is an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: Helmeted riders are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: A helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, at any speed.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if they wear a full-face helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can permanently damage your hearing, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it signals a hazard on the right side of the road. Signals like this help riders communicate when riding in groups.
